Some facts since the good Congressman will not give a complete picture ….

During the Biden administration, an estimated $98 billion was used for enhanced Affordable Care Act (ACA) subsidies through specific legislative actions. 

This total is composed of two primary legislative actions:

•The American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA), enacted in March 2021, spent an estimated $34 billion to temporarily increase the amount of premium tax credits and remove the 400% federal poverty level income limit on eligibility.

•The Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), enacted in August 2022, extended these expanded subsidies through the end of Calendar Year 2025 at an estimated cost of $64 billion. 

Overall, from fiscal years 2021-2024, refundable ACA premium tax credits totaled about $337 billion, which was approximately $143 billion higher than the pre-Biden administration baseline, according to some analyses. The administration has also requested a permanent extension of the enhanced subsidies, which the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) and Joint Committee on Taxation (JCT) estimate would cost an additional $383 billion over the budget window
